stem: Veer draws three square-dot pictures in order: a $1$-by-$1$ square of $1$ dot, a $2$-by-$2$ square of $4$ dots, then a $3$-by-$3$ square of $9$ dots.

parts.text: Which claim correctly names how the next picture should be drawn?

options.text: The next picture is a $4$-by-$4$ square of $16$ dots, continuing the $n$-by-$n$ square pattern.
Any larger cloud of dots works, because greater size alone continues the pictures.
Drawing the next picture is what creates the square-number list in the first place.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Each picture is an n-by-n square of dots, so the next term is the 4-by-4 square with 16 dots.

teacher.key_rationale: The pictures encode square numbers through an n-by-n grid. Size alone omits that construction. Saying the drawing creates the number list reverses the relation.
